samples.summary: Format painter (Cmd+Shift+C / Cmd+Alt+V) loses the ability to turn a flag OFF on the target, because source runs no longer carry an explicit `false`
samples.evidence: The painter snapshots the RAW run style at the caret — `this.styleBuffer = { ...this.getStyleAtCursor() }` (packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:869) — and applies it as a merge patch over the target runs (text-editor.ts:1013 → applyStyleToSelection → doc.applyInlineStyle). Previously a source run whose bold was toggled off stored `bold: false`, so painting onto a bold target merged false over true and de-bolded it. After `styleOffAsClear` the source run has no bold key, the buffer omits it, and the painted target keeps its bold — painted text no longer matches its source. Fix belongs in the painter (snapshot effective style, or fill absent boolean keys with `undefined`), not in `styleOffAsClear`.

samples.summary: In the collaborative store the re-merge #749 promises exists only in the local cache; the CRDT tree keeps the runs split, so it is lost on reload/remote re-parse
samples.evidence: `YorkieDocStore.applyStyle` updates its cache with `applyInlineStyleHelper` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:1707), which now merges the identical-styled neighbours via `normalizeInlines`. The tree mutation (yorkie-doc-store.ts:1884-1890) only calls `styleByPath`/`removeStyleByPath` and never merges inline nodes, and the parse path has no inline normalization (contrast `parseBlockStyle` → `normalizeBlockStyle`, yorkie-doc-store.ts:217-226). After any remote-driven re-parse or reload the block is 3 inline nodes again: cache and CRDT disagree on run structure, and the model-level invariant asserted by the new docs test does not hold in the store real documents use. It also widens the cache/tree index divergence relied on at yorkie-doc-store.ts:1570-1571, where a cache-derived `inlineIndex` picks `targetInline` while tree edits use tree-derived indices.

samples.summary: DOCX export cannot express the one case the new rule keeps `false` for, so the named-style override is silently dropped on export
samples.evidence: The change makes an explicit `false` load-bearing in exactly one situation (the block's named style supplies the flag). The exporter emits run properties only for truthy flags — `if (style.bold) parts.push('<w:b/>')` / `if (style.italic) parts.push('<w:i/>')` (packages/docs/src/export/docx-style-map.ts:58-59) — and never `<w:i w:val="0"/>`, so a Heading 6 run whose italic was toggled off exports with no run-level italic and Word re-applies the style's italic. Pre-existing gap, but now the only representation of the override.

samples.summary: `styleOffAsClear` adds a per-block `findBlock` lookup on the hottest write path, which can degrade to a full recursive document walk per block for cell-rectangle toggles
samples.evidence: `styleOffAsClear` runs inside both visitors (document.ts:377, :431), so a toggle-off does one `findBlock(blockId)` per visited block. `findBlock` (document.ts:176-186) scans body/header/footer and then `findBlockInCells`, whose fallback is a full recursive `walkCellsForBlock` over body + header + footer (document.ts:214-220) whenever `_blockParentMap` (rebuilt only at layout) lacks the id. For `applyInlineStyleToCells` over a large table selection that is quadratic on every B/I/U/S off press; resolving the defaults once per table/block-type would avoid it.

samples.summary: Comments and an agent charter still document the old docs contract ("docs leaves an explicit `false` behind") after this change removes it
samples.evidence: verify-hunt-oracles.mjs:592-594 justifies the sheets round-trip oracle with "where this surface DIFFERS from docs, where the same round trip leaves an explicit `false` behind (#749, #793)" — no longer true, so the fact it exists to keep checked is stale (the assertion itself still passes). The same stale claim is handed to an agent at scripts/agent/charters-ui/sheet-author.md:85, and packages/frontend/src/app/harness/hunt/bridge.ts:56-61 still describes #749 as an open defect the reader exists to expose.

samples.summary: The `DocStore.applyStyle` interface contract still does not state that a key set to `undefined` means "remove it", which every toggle-off now depends on
samples.evidence: `Doc.applyInlineStyle` now relies on stores honouring `{bold: undefined}` as a deletion, but store.ts:75-81 documents only "Apply inline style to a character range within a block", while the neighbouring `applyCellStyle` documents the opposite convention ("Additive only — setting a property to undefined will not remove it", store.ts:117-118). Both current implementations comply, so nothing breaks today; a third implementation would silently make every B/I/U/S toggle-off a no-op.

samples.summary: If `findBlock` cannot resolve the block, `styleOffAsClear` silently treats the named-style defaults as empty and clears the flag
samples.evidence: document.ts:408-412 falls back to `defaults = {}` when `findBlock(blockId)` returns undefined, converting the toggle-off into a key clear even for a block whose named style supplies the flag — exactly the visual no-op the exception exists to prevent. Reachable only if a visitor yields an id `findBlock` misses (e.g. a cell block created since the last layout whose parent table is also unresolvable); `walkCellsForBlock` covers most such cases, hence low confidence.

finding.summary: Format painter (Cmd+Shift+C / Cmd+Alt+V) loses the ability to turn a flag OFF on the target, because source runs no longer carry an explicit `false`
finding.evidence: The painter snapshots the RAW run style at the caret — `this.styleBuffer = { ...this.getStyleAtCursor() }` (packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:869) — and applies it as a merge patch over the target runs (text-editor.ts:1013 → applyStyleToSelection → doc.applyInlineStyle). Previously a source run whose bold was toggled off stored `bold: false`, so painting onto a bold target merged false over true and de-bolded it. After `styleOffAsClear` the source run has no bold key, the buffer omits it, and the painted target keeps its bold — painted text no longer matches its source. Fix belongs in the painter (snapshot effective style, or fill absent boolean keys with `undefined`), not in `styleOffAsClear`.

verdict.reason: Verified independently. The painter snapshots the RAW run style (text-editor.ts:869 → getStyleAtCursor at 2949 → caretInlineStyle with withStyleDefaults=false, caret-style.ts:46-66, returning only `{...inline.style}`), and applies it as a merge patch (text-editor.ts:1013 → applyStyleToSelection:2935 → Doc.applyInlineStyle document.ts:375-380 → memory.ts:213 → mergeInlineStyle block-helpers.ts:316-325, where absent keys are left untouched). The new invariant removes the very key the painter depended on: toggleStyle writes `bold: false` (text-editor.ts:2881-2893), styleOffAsClear rewrites that `false` to `undefined` (document.ts:399-418), and mergeInlineStyle DELETES keys whose patch value is `undefined` (block-helpers.ts:321-323). So a toggled-off source run now carries no `bold` key, the buffer omits it, and painting onto a bold target cannot de-bold it — painted text diverges from its source. The path is reachable (shortcuts-catalog.ts:45-46; exercised by backward-selection-toggle.test.ts:815) and nothing normalizes the buffer. The design doc documenting the invariant (docs/design/docs/docs-font-controls.md:244-283) lists the affected pieces and explicit out-of-scope cases but never considers this stored-buffer consumer. This is a consumer outside the diff left inconsistent by a changed contract — in-lane for blast-radius, major impact, no refutation ground (code is present as described, no guard makes it unreachable).

finding.summary: Named-style exception writes a real `false` that survives a block-type change / paste, re-creating the #749 dead flag outside the new guard
finding.evidence: `styleOffAsClear` (document.ts:394-418) deliberately KEEPS `italic: false` when the block's named style supplies the key (Heading 6). Nothing re-normalises that run when the block stops supplying it: `Doc.setBlockType` (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:456) forwards straight to `store.setBlockType`, which only rewrites `type`/`headingLevel`/`listKind` and leaves `block.inlines` untouched — so Heading 6 → paragraph leaves an explicit `italic:false` in a paragraph whose style supplies nothing, i.e. exactly the dead flag the change exists to eliminate (unmergeable by `inlineStylesEqual`/`normalizeInlines`, and pinned against a later style redefinition). The same residue travels through the internal clipboard, which serialises whole `Block`s with run styles verbatim (packages/docs/src/view/clipboard.ts:10-23, 51-60) — copy Heading 6 text, paste into a paragraph, and the `false` lands there. Both paths bypass `Doc.applyInlineStyle`, the only place the demotion happens. Fix belongs either in `setBlockType`/paste normalisation or in a read-side rule that treats a false-with-no-supplying-style as clearable.

verdict.reason: All cited code reads as described. `styleOffAsClear` (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:399-418) skips the false→undefined demotion when the block's named style supplies the key (document.ts:413), and that branch is reachable because BUILTIN_STYLES['heading-6'].inline includes italic:true (packages/docs/src/model/named-styles.ts:91) with blockStyleId mapping heading/level-6 blocks to it (named-styles.ts:105-110) — so a real `italic:false` is written via store.applyStyle (document.ts:377/:431). Doc.setBlockType (document.ts:447-458) forwards to MemStore.setBlockType (packages/docs/src/store/memory.ts:242-271), which rewrites only type/headingLevel/listKind/listLevel and block spacing and never touches block.inlines (except the empty/structural cases at memory.ts:260-264), so Heading 6 → paragraph orphans that `false`. It is then genuinely dead: inlineStylesEqual compares italic strictly (packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:407) so normalizeInlines (packages/docs/src/store/block-helpers.ts:76-86) can never re-merge the run — the exact #749 harm the design doc names (docs/design/docs/docs-font-controls.md:256-261). The clipboard path also carries it verbatim: serializeBlocks/serializeClipboard (packages/docs/src/view/clipboard.ts:10-13, 30-36), deserializeClipboard (clipboard.ts:38-49) and cloneTableCells (clipboard.ts:57-62) copy run styles with no normalisation against the destination block's style, and the only two callers of styleOffAsClear are document.ts:377 and document.ts:431. The one plausible refutation — the spec's out-of-scope note at docs-font-controls.md:280-283 — covers only `false` flags already stored by older builds, not flags newly created by the named-style exception and later orphaned, so it does not license this path. Severity (major vs minor, since the render is visually unchanged and the flag self-heals on the next toggle) is arguable, but that is a severity question and doubt keeps the finding.

finding.summary: Hyperlink runs are a second place where an explicit `false` carries information, and `styleOffAsClear` does not exempt it — toggling underline off on a link is now a visual no-op.
finding.evidence: packages/docs/src/view/paint-layout.ts:387-391 renders `let showUnderline = style.underline ?? false; if (style.href) { ... if (style.underline === undefined) showUnderline = true; }`. So for a run with `href`, an ABSENT `underline` key means "paint the link default underline", and only an explicit `underline: false` suppresses it. `Doc.styleOffAsClear` (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:398-417) preserves `false` only when the block's *named-style* defaults set the key (`resolveStyleInline(blockStyleId(block), ...)`); a hyperlink in a normal paragraph has no named-style underline, so the `false` is demoted to `undefined`. Result: selecting a link and toggling underline off (Cmd+U / toolbar U, whose write funnels through `Doc.applyInlineStyle`) now clears the key and paint-layout immediately re-applies the link's default underline — the user can no longer remove a link's underline, and the raw-style-based `getRangeStyleSummary` will report underline OFF while the canvas paints it ON (the exact toolbar/render disagreement issue #715 was about). The fix belongs on the new code: the exemption in `styleOffAsClear` needs to also keep `false` for `underline` when the slice being written carries `href` (or the paint default has to move into the resolved-style layer).

verdict.reason: The claimed code exists verbatim and the bypass is reachable. paint-layout.ts:387-391 treats an absent `underline` key on an `href` run as \"paint the link default underline\", so only an explicit `underline: false` can suppress a link underline (used at paint-layout.ts:445). `Doc.styleOffAsClear` (document.ts:399-418) exempts `false` only when the block's named style supplies the key (line 410/413) and has no `href` exemption, while `underline` is in BOOLEAN_INLINE_STYLE_KEYS (document.ts:39-46). The demotion to `undefined` genuinely deletes the stored key: mergeInlineStyle deletes undefined patch keys (store/block-helpers.ts:320-323) on the path Doc.applyInlineStyle -> store.applyStyle -> applyInlineStyle (document.ts:377, block-helpers.ts:367). The toggle is reachable from Cmd+U (text-editor.ts:884-887 -> 2887 -> 2935) and the toolbar (docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx:404). Link creation stores only `href` with no explicit underline (text-box-editor.ts:1189/1207/1221, editor.ts:2955), so nothing else keeps the key present. Net effect: underline-off on a hyperlink is stripped and the canvas re-paints the link default, and the raw-style summary (editor.ts:2644-2714) reports OFF while the canvas paints ON. This is a consumer outside the diff relying on the old \"explicit false\" contract — in-lane and major.

finding.summary: Format painter (Cmd+Shift+C / Cmd+Alt+V) silently loses its ability to REMOVE B/I/U/S now that toggle-off clears the key instead of storing `false`
finding.evidence: packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:869 captures the painter buffer as the RAW caret run style (`this.styleBuffer = { ...this.getStyleAtCursor() }`, and `getStyleAtCursor` is documented at :2942-2949 as raw run style), and :1013 applies it via `applyStyleToSelection(range, this.styleBuffer)` → `Doc.applyInlineStyle` → `mergeInlineStyle` (packages/docs/src/store/block-helpers.ts:316-325), which only merges keys that are PRESENT in the patch. Before this PR a run that the user had un-bolded carried an explicit `bold: false`, so copying its formatting onto bold text un-bolded it. With `styleOffAsClear` (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:399-418) the key is deleted from the run, so the painter buffer no longer contains `bold`/`italic`/`underline`/`strikethrough` at all and pasting the format onto bold/italic target text leaves the target's formatting in place. Neither call site was updated to compensate (e.g. by materialising explicit `false`/`undefined` for the boolean keyset when capturing). Fix belongs at the painter capture site, or by having the painter capture the full boolean keyset.

verdict.reason: Every claimed location checks out. text-editor.ts:869 captures the format-painter buffer as the RAW caret run style via getStyleAtCursor (documented raw at :2942-2951, implemented by caret-style.ts:46-66 which returns only keys physically on the run). text-editor.ts:1013 applies that buffer through applyStyleToSelection (:2921-2939) → Doc.applyInlineStyle (document.ts:375-380) → store applyStyle → mergeInlineStyle (block-helpers.ts:316-325), which merges only keys PRESENT in the patch and deletes on undefined — so an absent key cannot clear the target's formatting. document.ts:399-418 (styleOffAsClear, called from :377 and :431) now rewrites a caller-supplied boolean `false` to `undefined`, deleting the key from the run unless the block's named style supplies it; its own comment at :382-397 confirms runs previously stored an explicit `false`. Consequently a run the user un-bolded no longer carries `bold`, the painter buffer no longer carries it, and pasting the format onto bold/italic/underlined/struck text leaves that formatting in place. No compensation exists: BOOLEAN_INLINE_STYLE_KEYS appears only at document.ts:39 and :405, nothing materialises the boolean keyset at the painter capture site, and the apply path does no pre-clear. This is a consumer of the changed Doc.applyInlineStyle contract left unupdated in a file outside the guard's own logic — in-lane for blast radius and major (caller left inconsistent by a changed contract). No refutation ground applies: the code is present as described, reachable via the Cmd+Shift+C / Cmd+Alt+V keyboard handlers, and unguarded.

finding.summary: Toggle-off now emits a Yorkie `removeStyleByPath` op on the hottest editing path (B/I/U/S); if Yorkie history cannot reverse TreeStyleRemove, Cmd+Z after a toggle-off silently stops restoring the flag
finding.evidence: With the demotion in `Doc.styleOffAsClear`, every B/I/U/S off-toggle now reaches `YorkieDocStore.applyStyleInTree` with the key set to `undefined`, so `removedInlineStyleAttrs` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:144-163) returns the attr and `tree.removeStyleByPath(...)` runs at yorkie-doc-store.ts:1881 — previously only `styleByPath` ran for a toggle-off (the `false` was serialized), and `removeStyleByPath` was reached only by the rare removeLink / clear-formatting paths. Docs undo is Yorkie-history based (`this.doc.history.undo()` at yorkie-doc-store.ts:2611), so the reversibility of the removeStyle op is now load-bearing for the most common formatting action in the product. I could not verify the SDK's reverse-op support from this checkout (the Yorkie SDK is not installed in node_modules here); confirming needs a collab/integration run that toggles bold off and then undoes it against a real Yorkie doc. Fix, if real, belongs in the Yorkie store (emit a compensating style write) rather than in the new Doc code.

verdict.reason: The mechanical part of the finding is accurate: `removedInlineStyleAttrs` (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:144-163) returns `['bold']` for `{bold: undefined}`, and `applyStyleInTree` runs `tree.removeStyleByPath(...)` at yorkie-doc-store.ts:1888, reached from `applyStyle` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:1716) and `applyStyles` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:1760), which is where every B/I/U/S toggle-off from `Doc.styleOffAsClear` lands. Undo is Yorkie-history based (yorkie-doc-store.ts:2616-2621). But the speculative part — "if Yorkie history cannot reverse TreeStyleRemove, Cmd+Z silently stops restoring the flag" — is already directly guarded by an existing, non-skipped unit test: packages/frontend/tests/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.test.ts:214-228 ("applyStyle clearing a key → undo → key restored") runs against the real `@yorkie-js/sdk` document (imported at test:2, pinned 0.7.16 in packages/frontend/package.json:93), asserts bold is cleared after `applyStyle(..., {bold: undefined})` (test:220-221 — non-vacuous, since without the `removeStyleByPath` the merged `bold=true` attribute would survive), then asserts `store.undo()` restores `bold === true` (test:223-224) and `redo()` re-clears it (test:226-227). The whole style+remove pair runs inside one `doc.update()` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:1710-1717), so it is one undo unit, matching the single `undo()` in the test. The test file is inside the vitest `include` globs (packages/frontend/vite.config.ts:268), and the same file explicitly `it.skip`s the undo cases the SDK genuinely cannot reverse (test:244, test:300), showing unsupported cases are marked rather than left green. So the reversibility the finding calls unverified is exercised by CI against the real SDK, not merely asserted in a comment.
